scope: Focused primary-source discovery across robotics, human motion, games, driving, physical simulation/weather and world-model evaluation; reconsideration of pending entries where new release/schema evidence was found. All active records checked structurally; existing sources were not all manually re-read.
limitations: Finite discovery, not a proof that every qualifying resource worldwide has been found.
General web-search and GitHub connector transport failed; direct official HTTP pages, arXiv searches and repository APIs were used.
Paper-only pending decisions here reflect unresolved release/provenance, not an automatic rejection of all paper-only catalog entries.
No complete dataset downloads, sample integrity verification, simulator execution, license adjudication or experiment replication.
Existing 361 source-review dates are preserved; the new review date applies to the 59 additions/restorations only.
Only the three named REBOOT26 task schemas were inspected; the registry as a whole is not certified.

additions.reason: Paired MP4/HDF5 files align each video frame with joint and camera transforms in an episode-fixed coordinate frame. The release includes metrics for dexterous trajectory prediction.
The publisher identifies Beta as the full trajectory release and Alpha as its subset, and documents visualization of camera streams, robot states and actions. Beta release is dated 2025-03-01.

The data card documents one complete episode per Parquet file, matching per-camera episode videos, timestamp/frame/episode indices, robot observations and action fields. This establishes an action-aligned temporal data path.

The snapshot pairs policy-episode MP4s with 10,783 NPZ proprioception/action files; session metadata provides instructions, timestamps and outcomes. The data card explicitly dates this snapshot 2026-07-17.

Each example includes a real-robot rollout video, task instruction and terminal progress score. Temporal clipping creates partial-outcome examples; the test subset is RoboRewardBench. Inclusion concerns observed execution outcomes, not causal intervention claims.

The official card identifies real-robot episodes containing multiview observations, robot states, action chunks and rollout segments, including failures and corrections. This supplies action-conditioned physical transitions.

Official dataset metadata defines six-dimensional action and observation.state fields, top/wrist video streams, timestamps and frame/episode indices. These document aligned manipulation trajectories; the official VLAReplica repository names this SFT release.
The documented schema explicitly represents observations, actions, next_observations and terminal boundaries. Scripts reproduce the trajectories, and environment APIs expose step-wise transitions.

Controlled possible/impossible event videos test violations of four physical principles, with loaders and evaluation code for prediction-based models. The released split table separates debug, main and held-out sets.

The benchmark explicitly tests video world models for temporal/common-sense violations and adherence to physical laws, alongside instruction following, using released multimodal prompts and a defined judging protocol.

World generation is decomposed into sequential next-scene tasks with explicit camera trajectories. The benchmark evaluates camera adherence, geometry consistency and specified motion across generated sequences.

The protocol explicitly assesses world simulators in gaming, driving and robot manipulation. Its manipulative evaluation measures whether predicted situation-aware videos translate into correct controls in dynamic environments.

Action-annotated navigation loops return to previously seen locations via rotations, retraced paths and alternate paths. Scene Graph Consistency Score evaluates persistence of the generated scene across revisits.

The prediction stage uses controlled simulated environments to test mechanistic simulation, transitive inference and compositional inference, including object interactions and robot actions. Inclusion is explicitly limited to this predictive scope.

A unified action API and downloadable evaluation episodes support planning, execution and replanning in closed-loop tasks. Evaluation measures world-model utility in navigation and manipulation, not only visual quality.
Sequence folders contain time-indexed multiview RGB-D frames with matching SMPL and object registrations. These expose ordered human/object states and contacts rather than only static assets.

The release documents motion-captured dexterous manipulation with synchronized views and SMPL-X, MANO and articulated-object ground truth, supporting consistent motion reconstruction and ordered state trajectories.

The official toolkit provides the complete VRS-based hand/object tracking sequences and distinguishes them from the curated HOT3D-Clips subset. Tracking observations and 3D states support ordered trajectory modeling.

The release contains raw SMPL motion and processed per-joint positions/rotations for interacting people, with text annotations and train/validation/test splits. Its generation tasks operate on ordered skeletal trajectories.
The released data include mocap-derived skeletal/SMPL-X motion sequences with text and interaction-order labels, plus split files and sequence visualization tools.
The schema defines start/end frame IDs and per-frame SMPL pose, translation, 3D joints and contacts, aligned with multiview images. This explicitly establishes ordered interaction trajectories.

The official release provides interaction motion data and sequence visualizations, with human-motion generation conditioned on object motion and geometry. Its temporal motion targets satisfy the trajectory criterion.
The dataset documents synchronized Kinect and egocentric frames, sequence start/end frame IDs and 3D body motion annotations. These provide ordered human-state trajectories in scenes.
The benchmark explicitly evaluates embodied world models for physical plausibility and task coherence, with released ground-truth data and a multidimensional evaluation toolkit.

A defined world-model protocol tests scene revisits, terrain/object/social interactions, physical reaction and goal completion under three control interfaces. Released test cases support diagnostic evaluation beyond visual appearance.

The benchmark releases paired videos sharing an initial image and commanded camera trajectory, with human verdicts on action consistency, appearance and motion quality. It specifically evaluates camera-conditioned world models.

The toolkit uses spectral reference simulators to generate PDE trajectories and evaluates autoregressive predictions over rollouts. Initial fields and subsequent numerical states form identifiable physical input/target pairs.

Official scripts construct temporal nowcasting training and testing datasets from SEVIR storm observations, using a date-based split. The documented forecast task predicts future observed weather fields.
The benchmark supplies temporally indexed reference weather fields and baseline forecasts, with an explicit protocol comparing predicted future atmospheric states at forecast lead times.

The official workflow splits physical-event recordings into conditioning and held-out continuation videos and evaluates generated physical rollouts. The repository maintains original and Verified evaluation variants.

The official repository supplies pre-collected manipulation trajectories, seed-based demonstration collection and policy rollout evaluation in executable robot environments. It dates the original release to 2024-09-20.

The release provides task demonstrations, deterministic seed replay for collecting trajectories, and policy evaluation in the same manipulation environments. Its admission rests on action-conditioned interaction, not a generic memory label.

The GenAD release explicitly supports future driving-video prediction and provides a complete video list, consecutive-frame preprocessing and language annotations. March 2024 news confirms the release of this toolkit.

The official release supplies driving clips collected by a driving agent and executable CARLA policy evaluation with defined routes, driving success, efficiency and smoothness metrics. Version and split manifests identify the released data.

The official data specification organizes OpenScene/nuPlan observations into ordered Scene/Frame objects at 2 Hz for planning agents. NAVSIM evaluates planned future trajectories using explicit simulation-based safety and progress measures.

The official benchmark releases Franka Kitchen, WidowX and A1 data and matching executable environments for offline RL and online fine-tuning. State/image observations and control trajectories support action-conditioned dynamics.

The official schema explicitly defines obs, next_obs, action, reward, done and trajectory boundaries. CityLearn, Industrial Benchmark and MuJoCo tasks supply physical control transitions at multiple policy quality levels.

Released demonstration segments pair compressed screen observations with JSONL actions, environment statistics and an initial checkpoint. The documentation warns that missing uploads can create gaps between segments.

Dataset loaders separate lookback observations from future rollout targets, with documented tensor shapes and 16-step rollout MSE. The benchmark contains simulated physical-system evolution and an explicit future-state prediction protocol.
The official release pairs contextual motion sequences and gaze with a documented future-human-motion prediction task, a demonstration, sequence visualization and a full-dataset application route.

The official dataset describes spatially calibrated, temporally synchronized RGB-D cameras and joint tracking of whole-body SMPL-X and objects during interaction, establishing ordered human/object state trajectories.

The official card documents per-episode Parquet and camera MP4 files, robot observation/action vectors, timestamps and episode/frame indices in LeRobot format. This directly establishes aligned mobile-manipulation transitions.

The publisher explicitly releases a 1,000-hour batch and documents synchronized episode videos, tactile streams, 114-dimensional observation.state, 111-dimensional action and metadata. Some dimensions are placeholders, so users must inspect embodiment-specific validity.

Each simulation sample includes a before/after pair for an explicit object move, state-derived answers and optical flow/depth/masks. The release includes data construction and evaluation procedures, making the physical counterfactual target identifiable.

The benchmark varies one scene factor at a time and supplies reference continuations for fall, collision and occlusion. Multiple physical-parameter rollouts share conditioning signals, enabling explicit outcome and counterfactual-consistency evaluation.

The StarCraft II schema aligns step/action records with current and next observations, timestamps, frame indices and boundaries. Dota 2 and CS2 releases document replay-clock alignment, partial visibility and per-view files. Published manifests distinguish completed data from estimates.

The release anchors rollout evaluation to an annotated initial object inventory, then measures presence, identity and structural persistence with visibility reasoning and static/dynamic tracks. This is a dedicated world-model memory protocol.

The official release specifies camera_traj.npz, per-frame bilateral MANO parameters and validity, calibrated video and temporally localized atomic actions. These form ordered human-state trajectories and support predictive modeling.

The official release pairs timestamp files with camera/tactile streams and documents synchronized observation loading, manipulation data and reconstructed particle dynamics. Its world-model tasks predict subsequent object deformation under interactions.

The released Orchard ground truth supports target-time state prediction and frame-wise trajectory comparison against physics-derived targets. The evaluator defines repeated rollouts and state/velocity/trajectory metrics, beyond generic physical-law QA.

The official release provides collision sequences and a reconstruction/evaluation pipeline for generated rollouts, including temporal dynamics, momentum and kinetic-energy diagnostics. Admission concerns the specified world-model evaluation protocol, not visual collision classification.

The official card and construction toolkit identify initial observations, language instructions and ordered action/pose trajectories with evaluation splits. The pipeline derives navigation actions from six-degree-of-freedom camera motion.

Each episode contains an input and target image generated from compositional scene state under a defined transition rule. Train/test splits measure systematic generalization in an explicit minimal world-model prediction task.

The release documents validation/test sets and an AgiBot training set, with paired action-conditioned real executions including successes and failures. Defined metrics evaluate physical state, interaction alignment and multiview action coherence.

The official environment exposes reset and action-conditioned step APIs returning observations, rewards and termination, with robot safety costs and multi-agent variants. It can generate physical-control trajectories without relying on a model-only release.

The official driver obtains observations, invokes client.move_to, records execution results and refreshes observations before the next movement. This directly exposes action-conditioned transitions, resolving the prior uncertainty about whether evaluation was static only.

The official release maps named dynamic PDE datasets to download and temporal loaders. The NS-Sines card explicitly documents 20,000 trajectories with 21 uniformly sampled time steps and train/validation/test splits. The admitted collection is restricted to time-dependent systems.

The official release pairs gameplay actions and visual observations with timestamps, audio and transcripts. Ordered interaction traces and outcome annotations expose action-conditioned game transitions rather than dialogue-only state.

The official registry links named LeRobot task releases. Their actual meta/info.json files define action, observation.state, camera/depth videos, timestamp and frame/episode indices. The three inspected manifests report 60, 62 and 60 episodes respectively; schema inspection replaces the previous profile-only evidence.
